rule: The words of the Handover, made at build time and read by the Unity host; nothing here is written live and no line decides anything (GDD §09: text is a light layer, history is what the systems record). The host finds a line with lookup() and picks a variant with pickIndex() (contracts/missions/handover/text.schema.ts): same seed and same run, same words. Keys follow the engine: verbs are the panel verb ids, outcomes the rulebook outcomes (`suspicious` when the person reports the approach), refusals are text codes found by lockOf() because the engine returns free text. People are named only Inez and Vale; everyone else is a role. Civilians are never the payload: no line asks a civilian to die, fight or be used as a weapon. Lines that name Halcyon are pending Sky (a Story proposal): ship the `unnamed` cliffhanger until Sky decides. Inez and the door guard are lovers (the Story spine; Sky, 2026-10-15): her debt is her need (Help), her secret is the guard (Pressure threatens to expose it). Written plainly and with tact, never explicit.

tone.world: An alternate 1950s that found atomic power centuries ago: 1950s manners and speech, centuries-ahead machines, no thinking machines or networks. Optimistic on the surface, coercive underneath: the city is polite, orderly and watching. Speech is plain, short and spoken; no period slang to dress it up, no modern internet speech.

voices.scout: energetic and chatty: quick, warm, short full sentences to her own cell; first to spot things and glad to say so; says plainly what is where and when; never wrong, never a joke to decode
voices.fixer: warm and persuasive: reassures, says "we", puts people at ease; steel under the kindness
voices.tech: calm and practical: procedure, minutes and what is tied to what; patient, a little dry about old wiring
voices.enforcer: dry, older, few words: one to four words where he can; gallows humour, never a speech
voices.waitress: Inez: warm café patter, quick, tired about money and the lender; her temperament shows in what she will and won't take
voices.driver: Popovic's official driver: gruff and practical; cars, wages, schedules; calls Popovic "the Councillor"
voices.guard: the door guard: officialese, clipped, the post and the rules; a mercenary one talks bonuses and "off the clock"
voices.councillor: Popovic: formal and pompous, then frightened; loyal blusters, mercenary bargains, fearful begs
voices.rivals: cold and businesslike: a contract, a schedule, no names
voices.patrol: a clockwork patrol: fixed polite phrases that mean orders ("Walking is encouraged. Running is noted.")
voices.security: the response unit: crisp, loud, procedural
voices.watcher: a person in the camera room, speaking into a handset: reports what the camera shows
voices.crowd: passers-by: startled, short, human; they never fight and are never used

pick.rule: variant index for the n-th use (0-based) of a key in a run: for i = 0..n, at = fnv1a32(seed + "|" + key + "|" + i) mod count, and if at equals the previous use's variant (count > 1) then at = (at + 1) mod count. fnv1a32 is the rulebook's (contracts/rules/rulebook.ref.ts, 32-bit FNV-1a over the UTF-16 code units). The key is event/verb/speaker/outcome/temperament/about with absent parts skipped; `seed` is the run's seed string. The line is the entry lookup() finds: every field an entry names must equal the query's, the entry naming the most fields wins, file order breaks a tie.

briefing.title: The Handover
card: Councillor Popovic has a file on us. Security gets it tonight.
At shift change he carries it out of the Civic Records Office.
We take him alive, get him into our getaway car and drive off.
Quietly, if we can. Others want him too, and this city notices noise.
We have $100,000, four people, and until 5:50, or 8:10 if we turn his driver.

page.rule: Brief 070 (Sky, 2026-10-26: the briefing as a full-screen page, modal until Begin; Glyph's mock briefs/070/glyph). Outside play, so the reading limits don't apply, but each way keeps to two sentences: its hint after the way's name (briefing.hints, the part after ': '), then `ways.<id>.line`. `when` is the plate beside the way's name, `target` the line under Vale's one fact (brief.json dossier.target), `ending` the line under the getaway car's still, `clock` the stations the page's clock shows (labels from briefing.timeline, unless `stations` words the mark for the page: Glyph R1 on 0.2.133, the 5:50 station is the short form, since the 5:20 station carries the condition; play's timeline keeps the full, true label), `cell` one line under each face, about this mission. `heads` the section heads (Glyph's mock; brief 070, Latch: the page showed none): `ways` keyed by how many ways the mission has (brief.json ways), so the head counts from the data; `where` over the plan, `clock` over the stations, `heat` beside the Heat word. `captions` a still's caption by its pin's place, where the target's name alone would not say where (Glyph N11 and R6: the pickup's words end at the service bay, so its still and legend name the service bay); other stills take targets.<key>.name. The target head stays less.briefing.target. Day and Night are off the page (Sky: night is not a toggle).
page.target: Comes out at 5:30 and leaves by car.

page.ending: Both ways end here: Popovic in the getaway car as it leaves.

cards.rule: The feed's cards for engine events no scene covers (Sky's review 2026-10-16, messages.html §1 D). Each is a title and one result in the player's words with the engine's numbers, never the engine's sentence (its log keeps that). A card with `sight` in-sight shows only when an agent can see the place, as a city scene does; `sight` always shows wherever the cell stands (brief 067: the rival car turning in off Orbit Walk is heard, never seen), and its `at` then only says what the card points at. A result that is a record is chosen by the engine state `pick` names. {who} is the person or watcher as names.targets says it, {agent} "the Scout"; the host capitalises the first letter after filling. Brief 013 (takedowns): a card says only what the cell has seen or been told. Three kinds: (1) the cell's own acts (the agent is there, so no `sight`); (2) things at a place the cell may not be near: `sight` in-sight, and `at` names the engine position the check looks at (the log carries none; the host reads it from the game); (3) the city's answer to an Alert, which the Alert pill and the street show: a card says that it came and when, never who made the report or why. `needs` routine: a cause the cell can name only once a Watch has taught the person's routine (a missed check in); until then report.landed speaks alone. Codes the engine builds (stash.container, stash.door) are one card keyed by the prefix. A spoken line of an event shows with that event's card or scene, so it follows the same sight rule: a line is never shown when its card is hidden. Brief 014 (less reading): every card has a `fate`: beat (a one-line feed beat, `beat`; at most ten distinct lines in the file), icon (the street shows it: a marker, ring, lock or pip), alt (history only, behind L), debrief (the end says it). A card with no beat is never a card on screen; its title and result are the history lines.

debrief.rule: Brief 096 (Sky 2026-11-04: "the End card needs to be plain english and clear but not too formal"): `cause` words the end card by the engine's reason, never one line per code: cause[Game.FailCode][key], the key FailCause.Why, except sealed (FailCause.Car: held, ready, empty, else unknown) and withdraw (its why). `head` is the title, `line` the sentence under it ({by} {agent} as less.failcam, {holders} as names.holders), and `story` names lines of `story` that follow "Popovic reached the getaway car." in the route, so the story runs to the end ({holders} is Game.CarHolders() at the end; a line with {holders} and none is left out). A cause with no entry (why unresolved) falls back to less.end.fail and briefing.fails. Once wired it replaces less.sealed.line, less.sealed.story and less.closedIn.line, which say the same. The end card in the player's words, by the ids of sim Debrief.cs (route, assets, investigation cause) and the engine's named-witness:<role>. A failure with a line in briefing.fails takes that line's first sentence as its headline and the whole line as its result; the Fixer's spoken fail or win line sits under it (events fail, win). An id with no sentence here is not shown. The replay verdict and hash are never player text. brief 014: the Standing line, one per district (rulebook debrief.lines.standing: district, from, to, band, cause, who). `line` is filled by the host from the debrief's fields: {district} is the district's name, {band} is bands[band], {from} and {to} are signed (+3, 0, -1), {cause} is causes[cause] filled with {who}, the person's name. The seen and found causes say what the city saw or found, with no name. The word causes are rumour, not fact the cell watched: they begin Word is, and name no face, place or time.

rules.source: briefs/011/motive-fights.md §8 (Motive); words by Fable; each line fits Glyph's 110 characters
rules.one: One at a time, in priority order, lowest number first (H14, H16 and H15, the end steps, are -4 to -2: they win over every other hint, H17 and H13 included, when their trigger holds; their triggers never hold together; H20, Drive the car round (brief 059), is -7: it wins over H16 while the getaway car is still at the square, so the Take is not offered with a long carry ahead; H17, the fight hint, is -1, behind H15 so that Put Vale in the car wins while a fight holds the car, ahead of H13; H21 and H22, the control tips of brief 067, are -8 and -9: see `tips`).
rules.once: Each fires once per run, and H hides the layer for good.
rules.idle: A hint shows only after the cell has given no order for 8 s (H13's door cause, H21 and H22 show at once).
rules.tips: Brief 067 (Glyph, batch 0.2.123): H21 (Holster to stop firing: press F; engine 0.35 one input, Cease fire and X retired) and H22 (Scroll to switch) are control tips, not steps. Each teaches one input at the moment the player has just met the need for it, shows once, at once (no 8 s idle wait: that would hide it for the whole fight or the whole crowd), rings nothing (the lock reticle and the stack tab are already on screen), and retires for good when the input is used. They are -8 and -9, below every other hint's number, so they show the moment their trigger holds; the idle flavour hints and the end steps return after them. H21 teaches F as the way to stop firing (text.test.ts holds it to the game's own binding); the file no longer names X.
rules.vanishes: It vanishes the moment its gone-when act happens, or when its trigger stops holding.
rules.words: Each line names an agent, a verb and a target, introduces one verb, and never names an approach, a time or a sequence.
rules.short: Brief 014: the line at rest is `short` (one imperative, one [noun] ringed, no agent); this long line is Alt and the relearn key. See `less.hint` for when it shows and retires.

Every long line elsewhere in this file stays and is the Alt text (hold Alt, or the history key L) or the debrief; nothing was deleted. `fates` says where each group of text goes; the rest of this block is the short forms and the one-line price grammar. intel.rule: Brief 016 (Intel panel, Glyph's redesign). The tooltip of a fact slot on a person's card is one fragment of one or two words that only names the fact; the host decides whether the cell has learned or been told it (the slot's rim says which), so no word here says how it is known. A fragment is never a sentence, has no gendered word and never says who told it. `need`, `temperament` and `secret` are keyed by the value the cast and the rulebook carry (needs.rules.json kinds, people.rules.json temperaments and secrets.list); a new value without a fragment fails the test. Brief 017: `need` and `secret` hold one fallback word per KIND, shown only while the need or secret is told and not yet heard; after Listen the host shows the record's own `label` from contracts/people/<plan>.needs.json, so no record's name lives here. `{name}` is the lover's name as the HUD shows it elsewhere: the given name for named people, the word the plus the role for role-named ones (Inez, the guard). `verb` is the word on the chip and on an unknown slot: what would teach it.

done.rule: Brief 043 (the done moment; Sky 2026-10-22: it is not clear when a task has completed and what it gained). Labels and numbers, never sentences. The plate is the portrait plate's word for 2.2 s after a landing or a cancel, keyed by the engine's outcome (the last part of turn.<approach>.<outcome>) or `done`; kept reads as turned. The gain chip shows one icon-plus-word line per fact, at most three, and the facts a Watch or Listen teaches are Intel's own fragments (less.intel: the need's record label, the temperament, Loves {name}) so the chip and the Intel panel never disagree; only the words in `gain` are new. Brief 058 (Sky, 2026-10-25): a looped camera shows the desk a clean picture, so a loop is never "dark": `camera-looped` is the Loop chip (the 2:00 countdown rides the window marker), `camera-cut` the Disable chip, `camera-shot` the chip of a camera shot out, `parked` the chip of a car Drive that has arrived and `timetable` the chip of a Watch on the rival crew (brief 059: the street draws the three facts it teaches, the next move, the spring ring and the follow line, so the chip names them as one; a bare noun on the thing, as `rounds` is on the patrol). A window marker is an icon with a count or the doer's face; `close` is the pop on the thing when the window ends, by the marker's kind. Unlock-row pills are the verbs' own ring labels (actions.ring-*), shut ones struck through, so they carry no words here. Cancel: the tag before is `tag` or `tagCost`, the pop after `pop` or `popCost`, {verb} the ring label of the order dropped, {cost} one of `cost` by the engine's cancel cost (lost, aborted, released, staff-report, vale-reports, ends; the rest are free and show no cost; `drives-on` is no cancel at all, engine 0.33.1: a Drive under way is refused `car-driving`, so Cancel is hidden for the driver and the riders and no tag or pop shows), {s} the seconds spent. Walking in: the plate shows `walk.plate` with {who} from `walk.who`; the pill and Alt show `walk.line` with {target} from names.targets and {verb} the ring label. The old 'serving a table, back in {s} s' refusal is retired (engine 0.23: the agent walks up to the server at the table). Focus (engine 0.35 one input, the sticky focus, GDD section 10): the plate under a focus that waits, two lowercase words by the engine's FocusOf state (aiming, walking-in, no-line, out-of-reach; firing shows no plate); no-line and out-of-reach say what the fire refusals say.

rules.what: Short scenes for the update feed (Sky, after playing): conversations between the people and the cell, overheard or played out, in the order of their beats. The log shows the first beat collapsed and all of them expanded; the result line is what the player now knows or has.

kinds.overheard: Watch or Listen lands: the target talks with the people around them (clerk, owner, customer, guard, driver). Watch learns the routine; Listen the need, the temperament and, for Inez, her secret.
kinds.approach: A turn order lands: the Fixer and the target, ending in the target's reply and the Fixer's reaction. Beats with `ref` are lines from `dialogue` (ack, arrive, reply, done, confirm), so a scene extends the exchange and never contradicts it.
kinds.call: The Fixer calls a turned contact: Inez calls the guard over and he leaves his post for her, to hear what she has to say. The driver has no call (brief 059): he acts on his own once turned.
kinds.city: The city does something the cell may see. `sight` in-sight: show it only if an agent is within 13 m with a clear line; always: anyone hears it (the bell). Brief 013: a city scene may carry `outcome` (what the cell sees a witness do: report, flee, check) and `about` (the person missing); the host finds it with lookupScene() on the event, then the outcome.

rules.less: Brief 014: a scene plays as speech bubbles at the speakers, not as a card. Overheard and approach scenes play every beat (what the cell learns, and the Fixer's drama, are in them); call and city scenes their first `less.feed.cityBeats`. `result` is the Alt and history line; a `beat` is the one feed line when the scene starts.
rules.pick: A scene is found by lookupScene(); a variant is picked by pickIndex(seed, key, n, count); a `ref` beat is picked by pickLine() with the same seed and n.
rules.story: Inez and the door guard are lovers (the Story spine; Sky, 2026-10-15). The cell learns it by Listening at the café; he takes his café stop to see her, and when the turned Inez calls him over he leaves the door, which is what the call scene shows. Her debt is her need (Help clears it); the guard is her secret (Pressure threatens to expose it, and she resents it). Written plainly and with tact; nothing explicit.
